decisions.name: 先河环保
reasoning: Broad policy/enforcement hubs triggered a search for monitoring/compliance demand, not an environmental-equipment sector screen.
H1 already showed grid-monitoring order execution contributing to growth, establishing real company conversion.

The Sep-28 Hebei '1+18' monitoring contract was RMB228.8m, roughly 29% of 2016 revenue, large enough to make a previously emerging monitoring/data-services pool materially relevant to consolidated results.
The stock was not strongly front-run immediately before the event: 20d excess versus CSI300 about -2.5pp and 60d excess about +5.4pp.
Valuation/expectation burden was high, so this remains Research rather than High-priority.

decisions.name: 中国铝业
reasoning: Supply-side reform and aluminum capacity cuts produced very strong real earnings conversion; H1 attributable profit rose roughly tenfold.
But this remained the company's existing core aluminum/alumina profit pool rather than a newly material business line.
The market had already aggressively repriced the cycle by Aug-18: 20d/60d/120d excess versus CSI300 about +21.3/+48.5/+26.2pp.
The economic thesis is correct, but expectation and price absorption are too high for a new entry at this checkpoint.

decisions.name: 中国国航
reasoning: The broad RMB-appreciation hub signal maps directly to Air China's USD liabilities and FX-sensitive earnings.
H1 financial statements quantify the bridge: a 1% RMB appreciation versus USD increases net profit/equity by about RMB290.6m; H1 had already swung from an FX loss to an FX gain.
By Sep-12 sell-side research had explicitly quantified this benefit and expected Q3 airline profit acceleration, so this is not an undiscovered emerging profit pool.
However, price absorption was low/negative: 20d/60d/120d excess versus CSI300 about -5.7/-13.1/-5.4pp.
The test therefore keeps this known-macro case as Research rather than filtering it out by label.
Steel/coal profitability recovery was real but already the dominant supply-side-reform narrative.
No additional company case was frozen that offered lower absorption and a distinct incremental earnings pool without duplicating the aluminum control.
Macro factory-output strength did not by itself establish a sufficiently specific company order/backlog reset before the holdout cutoff.
Do not convert strong industrial activity into a generic machinery trade.
The value-chain margin signal was plausible, but the frozen evidence did not isolate a cleaner incremental company bridge than the already heavily repriced core commodity cycle.
Capacity reduction alone did not prove sufficient demand/order-quality recovery at a listed yard within the holdout window.
Avoid treating sector consolidation as an earnings catalyst without company conversion.
